desc: Parse input, separate fixed values from -1 entries in A and B, and count wildcards (wA,wB) and fixed counts (pA,pB).

Derive feasibility for a fixed sum S: a matching of size M(S) between fixed A and fixed B exists with a+b=S, and perfect assignment is possible iff M(S) >= T where T=pA+pB-N; also require S >= L=max(max fixed A, max fixed B); if T<=0 the answer is always Yes.
Prove that for T>0 any feasible S must equal a+b for some distinct fixed A value a and distinct fixed B value b, so candidates are the O(pA*pB) pairwise sums (filtered by S>=L).
Derive M(S)=sum over distinct v of min(cntA[v], cntB[S-v]) and the exact acceptance test M(S)>=T.
Implement candidate-sum enumeration with per-sum aggregation (numpy broadcast/unique/bincount fast path plus pure-Python dict fallback), with early exit once a sum reaches T.
Verified all three public samples (Yes, No, No) and hand-checked edge cases (T<=0, all-wildcard, duplicates, N=2, zeros, adversarial many-distinct-sums).
